## AI-Generated Details

Prepared with Codex from the author's GraphPP multiplexing design.

Interleaved1F1BCombined uses the companion native PyTorch schedule:
https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/201439

Multiplex independent forward/backward graphs without EP token chunking or
capacity division. Explicit source annotations preserve ownership and positional
ABI. Consume the earlier native request/input validator, tensor/mutation
dependencies and page FIFO/lifetime contracts. Existing pipeline code retains
receives, unshards, sends, gradient accumulation and callbacks.

Communication launches, including paging, prefer ready complementary-source
work among equally ranked nodes. The shared early-launch/late-wait scheduler
prefers launch-enabling compute over unrelated wgrad; no second scheduler or
timing heuristic. Consume the earlier high-priority streams, operation-only
resource controls, vectorized pager, live-prefix calibration and no-AC policy
unchanged. The eager terminal-wgrad reservation is empty for unchunked PP.
This update only rebases the PP consumer; it does not overwrite those owners.

Native varlen Flash selects FA4 on Blackwell. DualPipeV retains its native
two-stage-per-rank V mapping, full backward for combined actions and separate
dI/dW for bubbles. dI retains the required live-ins until dW produces parameter
gradients. There is no copied schedule, patched backend or synthetic acceptance
path. DeepEP and full-graph Inductor remain excluded.

Full-step CUDA capture includes every microbatch's distinct routing state.
The native experimental `graph_capture_record_stream_reuse` setting releases
storage only after graph dependencies prove asynchronous uses joined; keep it
equal in both arms. It does not replace annotations, ownership or waits.

## Verification

Combined-stack tree `9542fd0f3872179b0f9c4042a8bb85107f56908b` passed all 3 full-
CUDA numerical comparisons, including combined PP no-AC and DualPipeV paging,
plus 69 focused cases. The latest local 16B combined PP profile preserves all 40
loss/norm pairs and active/reserved memory. Device traces exercise native FA4,
HybridEP, copy/pop, grouped GEMM and whole-step replay; no new scale result is
inferred from these local checks.

Latest completed 16B scale measurements at the preceding source gave forced
PP 1.106x and real PP 1.102x, with exact 7 paired loss/norm samples. They used
PP2/DP=EP32/TP1, 4 stages per rank, 64 microbatches of 4 sequences, length 1024,
balanced 1x/real-routing 8x capacities, no AC/SAC, paging in both arms and full
CUDA graphs; 60 steps, throughput 11-50, profiler 59-60 and snapshot 60.
Those results retain exposed EP/page work and do not meet 1.2x. The next four
overlap-only 32/64-GPU runs remain pending. PyTorch is unchanged; owned lint/doc
hooks passed, with the unrelated video typing baseline outside scope.

 ### Compiler Optimizations
 
@@ -269,6 +268,58 @@ Current limitations:
 - The token count must be even.
 - Additional overlap or sharding modes require their own loss and trace checks.
 
+### Pipeline Communication Overlap
+
+Pipeline overlap uses `Interleaved1F1BCombined` or `DualPipeV` and graph
+multiplexing, not EP token chunking. `Interleaved1F1BCombined` adds one warmup
+forward, then pairs an independent
+forward and backward as an explicit `OVERLAP_F_B` action. Both actions' receives
+and parameter unshards precede the pair; normal send, gradient accumulation and
+reduction ownership remain in the existing pipeline schedule.
+
+`DualPipeV` uses the upstream V-shaped mapping with exactly two stages per
+rank. Its combined actions use full backward; separate input-gradient and
+weight-gradient actions fill the bubbles. Their saved activations remain live
+until weight backward completes. The focused HybridEP recipes use native
+varlen attention for both schedules, including actual dI/dW graph splitting.
+
+```python
+config.parallelism.pipeline_parallel_schedule = "Interleaved1F1BCombined"
+config.compile.enable_graph_pp_comm_compute_overlap = True
+config.compile.ep_overlap.enabled = False
+config.compile.inductor_compilation = "regional"
+config.training.disable_cuda_graphs = False
+```
+
+Use non-blocking `HybridEPTokenDispatcher` capacity. Enabling the GraphPP pass
+selects explicit asynchronous native launches/waits without splitting tokens
+or dividing each microbatch's capacity. Configure `sac_and_paged_stash` to
+include page operations. Source graphs retain explicit forward/backward
+ownership when multiplexed. The pass validates native request/input lifetimes,
+preserves tensor/mutation and paging queue dependencies, launches ready
+communication early and postpones waits behind independent compute.
+Each EP or paging launch gives ready work in the opposite source graph priority,
+including its ready completion waits, instead of draining one source first.
+Full CUDA capture covers the entire pipeline forward/backward step, including every
+microbatch's distinct native routing state.
+
+For long multistream captures, PyTorch's native allocator can reclaim storage
+after graph dependencies prove its asynchronous uses have joined:
+
+```bash
+PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF=graph_capture_record_stream_reuse:True
+```
+
+This upstream option is experimental. Without it, cross-stream frees can wait
+until capture ends, growing the graph pool with the microbatch count. Keep the
+same allocator setting in matched comparisons; it does not replace request
+ownership, stream joins, or the explicit overlap annotations.
+
+The pass can be disabled with `compile.disable_passes =
+["graph_pp_comm_compute_overlap_pass"]` for a same-schedule comparison. Without
+combined actions, the requested overlap emits a warning. Full-graph Inductor
+and DeepEP are outside this feature's scope.
+
